payload.description: Apply a source correction to its saved graph without changing source text or permissions.

payload.source_contract: One user-scoped understanding graph supplied through current evidence-owner relations; personal source paths and content are never package DATA.
invariants: every derived claim resolves to an exact source revision and span
facts observations inferences hypotheses counterexamples and test outcomes remain distinct
meaning series format channel duration audience reusable job and revision are independent refs
source corrections invalidate only exact dependents
applicable operations retain owner disposition and output refs
attention is a derived projection and never a second editable state store

payload.name: write-understanding-graph
payload.description: Write one user-scoped Understanding graph under the evidence owner's fixed address family. Source identities, meanings, decisions, consumer contracts, outcomes, and corrections remain caller DATA; this action owns only their canonical record boundary.

payload.why: artifact bytes are reached through the guarded reader, and the identities that came before it (`cas_address`, `multihash`, and direct imports of the local-files and cas-store packages) each name a route that no longer holds the access decision. A source that still spells one of them either takes that route or is about to. This rule replaces a hand-rolled directory walk in this package's own tests, which is the shape it had to take while the rule collector read a single manifest: a package could not declare a rule about its own source, so eighteen packages wrote the walk instead. Two lessons from that walk are kept here rather than rediscovered. Generated output is not source, and without excluding it the walk reported ten `built-stored-bytes/*.source-closure.json` build receipts as offenders, because a receipt legitimately records the multihash of what it built. And a token walk measures VOCABULARY rather than behaviour, so a file that holds these names behind an imported constant passes while doing exactly what the rule forbids; that is not hypothetical, it is how `migrate-artifact-reference-target.ts` passed this check while being the one file that actually recognized the legacy fields. Treat a clean run as evidence about spelling, and pair it with the reachability rules that judge routes.
payload.message: an active artifact source names a retired byte identity, which is a route that no longer carries the access decision

payload.why: a relation address is composed by the target that WRITES a row and recomposed by the target that READS one, to check a stored row sits at an address matching its own fields. Those two spellings must be the same string or the reader rejects rows the writer legitimately produced. They were separate copies until 2026-09-05 (`materialize-artifact-target.ts` composed, `read-guarded-artifact-target.ts` recomposed inline), so either could have been edited alone, and the split would have surfaced as a stored-row integrity error rather than as the code divergence it was. `relationAddress` in `read-data/content-media-evidence.ts` is now the only owner and is exempted BY PATH, because an exemption marker inside the text is something any file can grow. Tests are out of scope deliberately: a fixture that composes an address through the owner cannot detect the owner itself being wrong, and one suite must spell a hostile caller-chosen address literally to prove it is refused.
payload.message: this file spells the relation-address grammar instead of composing it through relationAddress, so the writer and the reader can drift apart silently

payload.why: a surface runs on the viewer's machine, so bytes it fetches are fetched with whatever authority that machine already has, and the access decision stays behind on the server unread. The guarded reader exists to carry the decision with the request, and a surface that calls the byte store directly bypasses it while looking like ordinary rendering code. The predecessor of this rule named EIGHT exact file paths, which is a list that goes stale the moment somebody adds a ninth surface and reports clean about it forever; the scope here is every `show/` directory instead, because `show/` IS the convention for what renders. Note the one file the enumeration named that this scope does not reach, `screen-arrangement/do-work/read-canonical-artifact-object-url.ts`: an object URL is a browser concept, so that file is a surface living in `do-work/`, and the honest repair is to move it rather than to write its path here and re-create the list this rule exists to delete.
payload.message: a rendering surface reaches the byte store directly, so the access decision never travels with the request

payload.label: Content Media Evidence
payload.description: Shared evidence-pipeline projection helper for content and media packages. Package data declares roles; surfaces consume generic projections.

payload.relation_rule: An inventory row is admitted only from the exact canonical materialized-relation shape: one canonical artifact source_ref, exact target_ref and role_ref values, owner context_ref, and one idempotency_ref. Receipt, state, error, semantic, path, and unknown relation fields are not materialized-result facts.
payload.observable_rule: A materialized result satisfies only its declared observable role_ref. Media type, display name, size, provenance, target identity, identical identity text, path, and semantic keys never widen that coverage.
payload.original_byte_rule: An inventory result never satisfies an immutable-bytes demand. Original-byte demands remain separate exact demands and must use the exact byte/range owners.
payload.paging_rule: A relation stream is evidence only as a complete cursor chain from first cursor null through each named continuation to final nextCursor null. A truncated chain cannot produce a smaller complete inventory.
payload.package_rule: Every admitted row names the requested package. Rows from another package are refused rather than borrowed.
payload.conflict_rule: relation_id is the relation identity. Exact duplicate rows merge; one relation identity with two different semantics refuses the entire inventory before any result is admitted.

input_contract.source: bounded-json-safe-browser-bytes, or engine-staged bytes plus an equal verified single-address CAS identity, with metadata and provenance in request identity
input_contract.idempotency_ref: owner-recomputed relation identity for browser bytes; verified content hash for engine-staged bytes

payload.name: content-media-evidence-create-relation
payload.description: Write one generic source-target-role relation record with opaque refs and owner-owned receipt/state/error refs.

payload.justification: User media content = truth (keep current). store_as:binary-blob directs the producer seam (WS3b C6) to store bytes as a binary CAS blob, NOT base64/hex TEXT in JSON (44GB studio, 1.33-2x text amplification).

payload.name: stage-local-path
payload.description: Generic workflow-native staging: copy one stable, canonical regular host file (native_ref) into CAS single-chunk and return its integrity_hash as an artifact address. Workflow equivalent of the proven browser-side stageContentMediaLocalPath helper (content-media-work-loop.ts:192). Single-chunk 16MB (== max_addressed_chunk_bytes) so integrity_hash is a real CAS address (avoids the multi-chunk phantom-hash bug the 4MB helper hits for >4MB files). Fail-closed >16MB until the process-engine multi-chunk blob_ref fix lands.

local_path_identity_policy.path: absolute canonical path with no symlink component
local_path_identity_policy.source: non-empty regular file reached through a canonical path with no symlink component
local_path_identity_policy.stability: device, inode, link count, byte length, modification time, change time, and mode remain exact across staging
local_path_identity_policy.readback: held source bytes stream through engine-owned capture into one immutable seed that is the addressed output
